definitions.explanation: The polite form of {名前|なまえ} (name), formed by adding the honorific prefix お. Used when asking about or referring to someone else's name in polite or formal situations.

examples.japanese: お{名前|なまえ}をお{聞|き}かせいただけますか。
examples.english: Could you tell me your name?

examples.japanese: こちらにお{名前|なまえ}と{住所|じゅうしょ}をご{記入|きにゅう}ください。
examples.english: Please write your name and address here.

notes:
One of the first polite expressions learners encounter. The お prefix makes {名前|なまえ} honorific, so it is used to refer to the listener's or a third person's name, not one's own.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- お{名前|なまえ}は？ — What is your name? (casual-polite)
- お{名前|なまえ}を{伺|うかが}ってもよろしいですか — May I ask your name? (very polite)
- お{名前|なまえ}をどうぞ — Your name, please

USAGE:
- At receptions, clinics, and service counters, staff will say お{名前|なまえ}をお{願|ねが}いします (your name, please)
- When filling out forms, instructions may say お{名前|なまえ} to indicate the name field
- Do not use お{名前|なまえ} when giving your own name; simply say {名前|なまえ} or {私|わたし}の{名前|なまえ}は～です
